title: skip_specs was set although the change is not documentation-only
resolution: The OpenSpec mapping says a change without capabilities sets skip_specs, as four earlier test-only changes did, and both requirements stay unchanged; design.md now cites that rule and those changes.

title: The change recorded no scenario results, which the requirement Recorded scenario results asks for
resolution: An evidence run of the suite on cc0a82ee wrote results.jsonl (8 rows, all passed), and the load and perturbation rows now name their uncommitted instrumentation.

title: The lost-cancel risk said the old test passed with code 0, though assertCancelled rejected it
resolution: The risk now says a lost cancel fails on the ended bound instead of on the code-0 assertion.

title: The self-check claimed no added wait, overlooking the held process's 50 ms release poll
resolution: The self-check and proposal now say no scenario bound or existing sleep was widened and name the 50 ms release poll separately.

title: The skip_specs decline left out that the agent task protocol states skip_specs more narrowly
resolution: design.md and the pass 1 entry name the narrower protocol text and say the change follows the OpenSpec mapping and the test-only precedents; Limitations lists aligning the texts as a follow-up.

title: The revision section did not name the evidence run and pass 1 record commits
resolution: The revision section lists every commit and says make verify on b6531977 ran with the pass 1 records uncommitted.

title: An infinite duration stood for the held mode and needed a JSON null round trip in the fixture
resolution: runMilliseconds is a ScriptedRun, a number or HELD_RUN ('held'), so the crash-before-ack fixture passes it through JSON unchanged.

title: The assertCancelled comment called every started process held, and the release comment read poorly
resolution: The comments now say a started process is held by c, e, and f, and that a release lets running or future held processes exit 0 until the next hold.
